rendered:
NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated within a pH window of about 10[1] to 12[2]. The window is this narrow because the metals do not precipitate together. Hydroxides of aluminum start precipitating at a lower pH than hydroxides of nickel and iron, which precipitate only beyond pH[3][4] 6[5]. The authors attribute this to the differing solubility product (Ksp) of the resulting hydroxides, which makes simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum challenging. Operating within that pH range is what allows NFA to be synthesized successfully as hydroxide precursors.[6]

To turn the precursors into cathode powder, the outflow from the reactor is first filtered, washed and dried to obtain the hydroxide precursors.[7][8] The dried hydroxides are mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.) and calcined in an O2-rich environment at temperatures >600 °C[9]. After calcination the NFA cathode powder is ready; it is cast into electrodes by roll-to-roll slot-die coating and assembled into cobalt-free LIB pouch cells.[10][11]
